patient_overview.name: Manuel Hilpert
patient_overview.description: Manuel Hilpert is a 40-year-old divorced warehouse worker from Trenton, New Jersey, living with his sister and her teenage son. He carries a long history of chronic migraine, chronic pain, dependent drug abuse (with a recent overdose in July 2026), unhealthy alcohol use, and newly flagged prediabetes and obesity. He speaks in a careful, numbers-first way—citing dates, doses, and lab values he's memorized from his chart—while agreeing readily with whatever the clinician suggests, though he rarely follows through. He comes across as cooperative and even eager to please, but a student will notice the gap between his nodding agreement and his actual day-to-day habits.

demographics.occupation: Warehouse order picker at a distribution center near Trenton
demographics.cultural_context: Manuel grew up in a working-class household in Trenton where food was simple, filling, and rarely discussed in terms of health—meals were about getting enough calories to get through a shift, not nutrition. He left school before finishing high school to start working, and he still thinks of doctors' numbers (A1c, blood pressure, milligrams) as the real language of health, something to memorize and recite even when he doesn't fully grasp what they mean. He values being easy to get along with and avoiding conflict, a trait that extends to never pushing back on his family or his doctors, even when he privately disagrees or doesn't follow through.

medical_history: Chronic intractable migraine without aura since 2000
Disease caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (2021-03 to 2021-05, resolved)
Removal of subgingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2023-02-27)
Removal of supragingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2023-02-27)
current_symptoms: frequent dull headaches and occasional severe migraines that keep him from eating regular meals
chronic low back and joint pain that makes standing in the kitchen or at work hard
occasional lightheadedness he attributes to 'low blood sugar' though he isn't sure
clinical_findings: BMI in the obese range with weight gain of about 1.7 kg since early 2023
blood pressure elevated at 141/91 at last visit
mild under-eye puffiness and tired affect consistent with disrupted sleep
dental wear and old plaque buildup noted at last cleaning, consistent with impacted molars and inconsistent dental care

medications.frequency: As-needed, carried for emergency use only
medications.adherence: Keeps it in his bag but has never had to use it; unsure of exact indication beyond 'allergic emergency'
medications.patient_concerns: Worried it might be expired since he never checked the date; otherwise doesn't think about it much

medications.name: Astemizole 10 MG Oral Tablet

medications.adherence: Inconsistent; sometimes forgets for a day or two, especially during migraine flares when he can't keep track of pills

food_preferences: convenience store coffee with lots of sugar and cream
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: late-night bowls of cereal or chips eaten alone after everyone else is asleep
finishing his nephew's leftover fast food 'so it doesn't go to waste'
skipping breakfast most days then overeating at dinner
drinking several beers on weekends with coworkers

nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly sweet tea and soda; says he 'forgets' to drink water during long shifts
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: On his feet all day at the warehouse but no structured exercise; chronic pain limits movement at home
nutrition_profile.substance_use: History of dependent drug abuse with a recent overdose in July 2026; drinks alcohol regularly on weekends, more than he admits to his doctor
nutrition_profile.sleep: Poor and irregular, often disrupted by migraines or pain, worse after a drinking night

psychosocial_profile.personality: Agreeable to a fault—says yes to every suggestion from staff, family, or coworkers, rarely voices disagreement, and as a result rarely changes anything about his routine
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Precise and factual, cites exact dates ('since 2007'), doses, and lab numbers he's memorized, but struggles to explain what the numbers mean for his daily choices

Stop having migraines interfere with work shifts
Stay clean this time, for real, after the July overdose
concerns: Losing his warehouse job if he misses more shifts for migraines or appointments
Being seen as 'the addict' by his coworkers
His weight creeping up even though he feels like he 'barely eats all day'
beliefs: If the doctor doesn't yell at him about it, it must not be that serious
Numbers on paper matter more than how he actually feels
His sister knows best about food because she's always cooked for the family
motivations: Wants to prove to his ex-wife and teenage daughter that he can get his life together
Fear of another overdose landing him back in the ER
Wants to keep his job and his own small bedroom in Donna's house
fears: Dying before his daughter is grown
Being told he needs to go back to inpatient rehab
Disappointing Donna after everything she's done for him
barriers: No control over what's cooked at home
Transportation problems that have made him miss medical appointments
Chronic pain and migraines that disrupt any routine he tries to build
Food insecurity—reports going without food at times during the month
Shame about binge or secret eating that he never mentions to providers
strengths: Shows up to appointments when transportation allows
Willing to recite and track his own numbers
Genuinely wants to stay sober this time
Good rapport with coworkers, sees people 3-5 times a week socially
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Lives with his sister Donna and her teenage son; family is present but tends to brush off his prediabetes and weight as 'not a big deal' compared to his addiction history
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Maintenance stage that is slipping—he made real changes a while back (cut back drinking, went to rehab in May 2026) but has been drifting back toward old habits since the July overdose

assumptions: The two recorded medications (epinephrine auto-injector and astemizole, an antihistamine) are long-standing prescriptions whose original indications Manuel no longer clearly recalls, consistent with moderate health literacy and passive medication management
Household of 3 is interpreted as Manuel, his sister Donna, and her teenage son, providing the 'family nearby who do not take the condition seriously' dynamic
The July 2026 overdose is the most recent destabilizing event explaining the slip from maintenance-stage changes made around the May 2026 rehabilitation
optional_details: Manuel keeps a small notebook where he writes down lab numbers from his after-visit summaries, though he doesn't always understand what to do with them
He has a nickname at the warehouse, 'Manny,' and gets along well with his shift crew, which is his main social outlet
